brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
An infusion of Minthostachys verticillata, a wild aromatic plant of the mint family, sold commercially by Argentine makers. Some chemotypes smell strongly of menthol.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: Gathering it in the Córdoba hills long supported local families, and scientists have warned since 1990 that wild native herbs there were at risk. The plant is now considered vulnerable and is harder to find. In Paraguay and northeastern Argentina it is sometimes confused with Mentha piperita.

vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
